entries.test: NVIDIA's 10-Q/10-K disclosure of the revenue share of its largest direct customers, which would show whether three customers account for about 54%.
entries.note: Only the 54% concentration figure can be checked cleanly. The guess about which ODMs these are is hedged ('likely'), and 'largely depends' is the author's interpretation.

entries.test: Hyperscaler bond spreads, borrowing terms and reported debt-market conditions in mid-2026, which would show whether their debt was getting harder or costlier to obtain.
entries.note: The point comes from Kedrosky, but Zitron states it in his own voice and adopts it. It reads equity sales as caused by tightening debt markets.
This is a claim about what the economics require, not a forecast of what will happen. The '$400 billion' is read as a combined figure, which fits his later 496% arithmetic.

entries.test: Microsoft disclosures or credible reporting on how its AI revenue run rate splits between OpenAI compute and Copilot or other products.
entries.note: The $8 billion Copilot figure is hedged ('maybe... at best'). The firm claim is that OpenAI compute makes up most of the run rate.
There is no shared test for what counts as having an 'AI story'.
'Not sustainable under any circumstances' has no agreed measure or time horizon. The insult in the second half is rhetoric.
Saying this is 'all' LLMs have given us, and calling it 'slopware', is dismissive exaggeration, not a measurable claim.

entries.test: Whether OpenAI and Anthropic both raise prices for their customers, for example on subscriptions or per-token rates.
entries.note: Only the 'inevitably' price-increase part is firm. The move to token billing and the subscription cuts are 'very likely', which is probability language.
This is about the labs' private intent ('by design', 'want'), and he hedges it with 'I think'.

entries.test: Whether compute spending by OpenAI or Anthropic, and the related cloud and NVIDIA demand, falls if either lab turns to profitability or cost-cutting.
entries.note: The setup is close to a counterfactual ('were to', 'assuming these things were possible'). It can only be tested if one of the labs actually changes course.
Phrases like 'ROI that's impossible to ignore' and 'super secret trick' have no shared measure. Calling Mythos 'bullshit' is a value-laden dismissal.
